s01.narration: Want to know who has already read the new policy? Hi, I'm Maria from the Sloneek team, and I'll show you how to upload and send documents.

s02.narration: Documents keeps contracts, policies and certificates in one place. Employees read and sign them right in the app.

s03.narration: In the left menu, under Company, I open Documents. They're managed by an administrator or a user with the Document manager right.

s04.narration: The list shows the folder, recipients, confirmation status and expiration. Folders are on the left, and All documents holds absolutely everything.

s05.narration: You create folders in Settings. I click Add folder and create a folder for HR policies.

s06.narration: I type a name and a short description. In User permissions, you can let selected people read the whole folder.

s07.narration: I click Create folder. The new folder shows up in the list right away, and you can file documents in it.

s08.narration: On the Approvals tab, you can turn on mandatory approval for documents that employees upload themselves. An administrator or document manager approves them.

s09.narration: In Notifications, you set how often Sloneek reminds people about unread and unsigned documents, and when it warns about an upcoming expiration.

s10.narration: Back in Documents, I click Add new document. You can create a document from a template or upload your own file.

s11.narration: You can upload for the whole company, for a single user, or in bulk for several people. I'll upload the policy as a company-wide document.

s12.narration: I type the name Remote work policy and pick the HR policies folder.

s13.narration: I upload the file, a PDF or an image. The private email toggle would also send the finished document to a private address, so I leave it off.

s14.narration: In Document owner, you decide who gets the document: the whole company, selected teams, or individual users.

s15.narration: For this example, I choose Selected users and pick James Miller from the list.

s16.narration: Under Expand, there are more options, such as the expiration date and a version label. For the version, I type 1.0.
s16.narration_tts: Under Expand, there are more options, such as the expiration date and a version label. For the version, I type one point oh.

s17.narration: The confirmation type can be Not required, Read confirmation, or Signature request. For a policy, a read confirmation is enough.

s18.narration: I tick the deadline and set it to fourteen days. Below, you can also set a deadline for new colleagues, counted from their first sign-in.

s19.narration: Finally, I add an accompanying message and click Confirm. Recipients get an email notification and find the document in the app.

s20.narration: The document is first in the list. The Status column shows how many people have confirmed it, so far zero out of one.

s21.narration: Clicking the name opens the detail. The preview is on the left, and on the right you can edit the name, folder, expiration or version.

s22.narration: The Confirmations tab shows the status for each recipient. Remind sends a reminder, and once it's read, you can download the confirmation here.

s23.narration: Contracts and amendments go to one person. I close the detail and choose Upload single user document.

s24.narration: I type the name, select James as the document owner, and upload the agreement file.

s25.narration: I expand the settings and choose Signature request. I set the deadline date two weeks ahead.

s26.narration: You can add more signers, such as a director, from your colleagues. To send the document to someone outside the company, use Add external user.

s27.narration: I click Confirm. The Status column now shows the signing status, so far zero out of one.

s28.narration: No need to write recurring contracts from scratch. In Templates, you prepare text with variables that are filled in from the employee profile.

s29.narration: For example, the name, position or start date. With Order of signatures, you decide who signs first.

s30.narration: Employees see their documents under My documents. In the Status column, they click Sign or confirm that they've read the document.

s31.narration: You can also see what was sent to whom in the employee profile, on the Documents tab. James has both new documents here.

s32.narration: Who can manage documents is set in the user profile, under Special user rights, by choosing Document manager.

s33.narration: Under the three dots, you can download, duplicate, archive, move to another folder, or delete a document. Archive outdated documents instead, because deleting can't be undone.

s34.narration: A final tip: with HR Workflows, Sloneek can automatically send new colleagues a document from a template, for example on their first day.

s35.narration: Now you know how to upload a document, send it to be read or signed, and track who has confirmed it. If something doesn't work, check the Help Center.

s36.narration: Less admin, more time for people. This is Sloneek.
